newsitem.title: USA: Life at high altitudes turns nails white - study.
newsitem.headline: Life at high altitudes turns nails white - study.

text.p: Living at very high altitudes for an extended period of time can make finger and toenails unusually white, two Toronto researchers said in a letter to Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.
Drs. Stuart Hutchinson and Smita Amin of the University of Toronto said high altitudes affected the cells that grow fingernails and toenails, causing the nails to be whiter.

They noticed the phenomenon in a 34-year-old man who spent six weeks climbing on Mt. Everest. During that time he was at an altitude where the air pressure was no more than half of what it is at sea level, and when he returned to sea level his cells started growing nail material with the normal colour.

"The width of the white band corresponded to the time the man spent at extremely high altitude, and the changes from low to high to low altitude were mirrored in the appearance of the nail," the doctors wrote. They said the white band showed that the shortage of oxygen at extremely high altitudes can disrupt the body in subtle ways.
